title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Head S budget reduction
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head S of the Estimates by $100, citing COVID-19 changes to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head S of the Estimates be reduced by $100." COVID-19 precipitated sudden and pervasive changes to how we work, why we work and what we want at work.

sections.label: Gig workers without CPF
sections.summary: Rapid growth of platforms has created a bigger group of gig or contract workers who do not have mandated CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The rapid growth of platforms or marketplace work has created a much bigger group of gig or contract workers and these workers do not have mandated CPF contributions.

sections.label: Foreign manpower skills weightage
sections.summary: The foreign manpower system must gradually pivot to give greater weightage to skills when issuing work passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, our foreign manpower system must gradually pivot to accord greater weightage to skills when giving out work passes.

sections.label: Mass resignations in developed world
sections.summary: Since early 2021, the developed world has seen workers resign en masse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Since the early part of 2021, the developed world has seen resignation of workers en masse.

sections.label: Employee wellness framework
sections.summary: A well-designed employee wellness framework covers mental health education and work practices, and legislating wellness within the Workmen Injury Compensation Act is neither envisaged nor wise now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A well-designed employee wellness framework looks at mental health education, work practices aligned to creating a safe and empowering environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We certainly neither envisage legislating wellness within the Workmen Injury Compensation Act, nor is it wise to do so at this point without understanding the issue better.

sections.label: National code for hybrid work
sections.summary: A national common code of practices is needed so workers and employers share understanding on making hybrid workplaces work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: What we need is to establish a national common code of practices so that workers and employers have a common understanding on how to make hybrid workplaces work.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines enshrined into law
sections.summary: Last year a big stride was made in signaling intention to enshrine the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices into law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Last year, we made a big stride in signaling our intention to enshrine the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices into law.

sections.label: Update on move
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to provide an update on this move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide us with an update on this move?

sections.label: Workers transition to green economy
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to outline plans to prepare workers to transition into the green economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry outline its plans to prepare our workers to transition into the green economy?

sections.label: Singaporean workforce value proposition
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked how it will ensure the Singaporean workforce remains a strong value proposition for businesses, especially MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry continue to ensure that the Singaporean workforce remains a strong value proposition for their businesses, especially that of multinational companies (MNCs)?

sections.label: EP applications complementarity diversity
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said MOM will assess EP applications on complementarity and diversity of the foreign workforce beyond qualifying salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance also mentioned in his Budget Statement speech that beyond qualifying salary, MOM will assess EP applications on the basis of complementarity and the diversity of our foreign workforce.

sections.label: Estimated loss for Singapore
sections.summary: For Singapore, the loss is estimated to go up to $143 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For Singapore, the loss is estimated to go up to $143 billion.

sections.label: Singaporean interest in jobs
sections.summary: Singapore may lack enough interested Singaporeans for jobs as other sectors compete for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, we may not have enough Singaporeans interested in such jobs, especially when other economic sectors are also competing for Singaporeans to join them.

sections.label: MOM study of sector work
sections.summary: MOM is asked to study the nature of work in sectors and split them into two categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can MOM consider a deeper dive into the nature of the work of various economic or social sectors that we are trying to drive higher productivity and differentiate them into two categories?

sections.label: PME policies and CPF ceiling
sections.summary: It asks for targeted policies, EP points system, and a review of the CPF contribution wage ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Following that, a set of differentiated and more targeted policies can be applied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To safeguard our Singaporean Core and curb discriminatory hiring, we must ensure that our Singaporean Professionals, Managers and Executives (PMEs) have access to a level playing field for jobs while, at the same time, balance companies' manpower needs in the immediate and longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am glad to note the upward revision of the Employment Pass (EP) and S Pass qualifying salaries announced during the Budget Statement 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, the eligibility criteria for EP focuses largely on the applicant's educational qualifications and salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I look forward to MOM taking into consideration the NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce's recommendation to further enhance the EP application process and include a points system which factors in, first, sectoral input; second, whether the employer has been hiring and developing local workers; and third, the diversity of nationalities within the companies, including seeking inputs from the tripartite partners, which is NTUC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The last time when CPF contribution wage ceiling was raised from $5,000 to $6,000 was six years ago on 1 January 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: With rising wages, especially of our PMEs and the Government's commitment during the last round of review to realign the salary ceiling to cover wages up to the 80th percentile of resident incomes, I wish to ask the Minister if MOM will consider a review of this contribution wage ceiling to ensure it keeps pace with income growth over the years?

sections.label: CPFIS returns and members
sections.summary: Long-term investments with risk should give higher returns than CPF rates, and 75% of CPFIS OA members profited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And it is, indeed, true that, generally, long-term investments with some risk should provide higher expected returns than the CPF interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We know that 75% of CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) OA members have earned some form of profits as of FY2020, but only 645,000 members are part of the CPFIS.

sections.label: Green sector workers
sections.summary: About 27,000 people work in the green sector, mostly in their 30s and 40s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While Singapore is accelerating the green transition, we must not forget that there are around 27,000 people working in the sector, a majority in their 30s and 40s.

sections.label: Shell Singapore capacity cut
sections.summary: Shell announced in November 2021 it is halving crude processing capacity at its Singapore hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Shell announced in November 2021 that it is halving its crude processing capacity at its Singapore hub and reducing fuel exports as it transits from fossil fuels to cut emissions and meet global low-carbon energy needs.

sections.label: LinkedIn green skills report Singapore
sections.summary: LinkedIn's first Global Green Skills Report on 22 February noted Singapore ranks 24th of top 25 countries in relative green skill intensity, below global average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: LinkedIn published its first-ever report on the state of the green economy in a Global Green Skills Report on 22 February, which noted that Singapore ranks 24th out of the top 25 countries in terms of relative green skill intensity, lower than the global average.

sections.label: Career Conversion Programmes sustainability reskilling
sections.summary: The passage asks how Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes will be augmented to reskill existing workers or train new hires in sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: How will Career Conversion Programmes being offered by Workforce Singapore (WSG) be augmented to reskill existing workers or train new hires in the sustainability sector?

sections.label: MOM petrochemical talent pipeline update
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will collaborate with companies to inform employees in the green transition and requests an update on MOM's domestic talent pipeline for petrochemicals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry collaborate with the companies within this sector to provide the necessary information for their employees in this green transition?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, ask the Minister to give an update on how MOM intends to keep a domestic talent pipeline for the petrochemical segments where petrochemicals are still envisioned to be used in the green future.

sections.label: Self-employed platform workers share
sections.summary: About a third of the 228,000 self-employed persons work for platform companies that assigned delivery or transportation work to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: About a third of the 228,000 self-employed persons (SEPs) work for platform companies that assigned delivery or transportation work to them.

sections.label: Median income employees versus gig workers
sections.summary: The median monthly income of resident employees in 2018 was $4,000 for permanent employees but only $1,322 for gig workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The median monthly income of resident employees in 2018 was $4,000 for permanent employees, but only $1,322 for gig workers.

sections.label: Platform Workers Advisory Committee update
sections.summary: The Advisory Committee on Platform Workers was set up six months ago, and the passage asks for an update on its progress and when recommendations will be public.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Advisory Committee on Platform Workers was set up six months ago, to look into better protection for platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can MOM provide an update on the progress of the committee and when we can expect the committee to make public its recommendations?

sections.label: Grab partners training interest
sections.summary: Grab says about 70% of partners want training and two-thirds hope to move to other careers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to Grab, and I quote, "Around 70% of our partners have expressed interest in attending training and skills development programmes to improve in their current role, while two-thirds of our partners hope to leverage skills gained to transit into other career fields." Do platform companies have to pay SDF for their platform workers?

sections.label: Public Service Division flexible work
sections.summary: PSD introduced FWAs, but the Government says hybrid work is not an entitlement and job requirements take precedence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: The Public Service Division (PSD) has introduced FWAs, but I read with grave concern the Government's stance that hybrid work is not an entitlement, and that the requirements of the job take precedence.

sections.label: Civil Service frontline functions
sections.summary: Minister Chan Chun Sing noted about 60% of the Civil Service is in frontline functions not suited to sustained home work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: In response to my Parliamentary Question in February, Minister Chan Chun Sing noted that some 60% of the Civil Service is in frontline functions, such as schools or the uniformed services agencies, which are not suited to be performed from home on a sustained basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: However, where operationally feasible, Public Service agencies can exercise flexibility and discuss FWAs with these officers.

sections.label: Victorian government flexible work default
sections.summary: The Victorian state government has made flexible work available by default to all employees since 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: For example, the Victorian state government has made flexible work available by default to all employees since 2021, focusing on service delivery outcomes, as well as employee support and well-being.

sections.label: Flexible work and SGUnited Skills
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to increase FWA adoption and cites Dylan, who got a data specialist role via SGUnited Skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I ask that the Government demonstrate a commitment to this new way of work and maintaining the attractiveness of Singapore as a place to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I hope the Government will take decisive steps to increase the adoption of FWAs, through legislating a baseline level of flexible work, conducting four-day work week pilots and allowing the Public Service a leadership role to implement more FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not being able to secure a long-term job, Dylan decided to take up the SGUnited Skills Programme at NUS-ISS in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After the six-month full-time Train and Place Programme, during which he was attached to AXA, Dylan successfully contracted to continue at AXA as a data specialist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package has supported thousands of Singaporeans like Dylan in several hundreds of companies during the pandemic.

sections.label: Updates on jobs and skills schemes
sections.summary: The speaker asks for updates on scheme outcomes, details of the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme, and welcomes the extended JGI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: So, can I ask the Minister for an update on the outcomes of these schemes so far?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: I welcome another new scheme that was announced by the Finance Minister, namely, the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme – Company Attachment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: Can the Minister share the details how this scheme would work and does he anticipate any difficulties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I am glad to hear that the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) has been extended to September 2022.

sections.label: Senior employment rate targets
sections.summary: Asks whether specific targets can be set for senior employment rate in growth industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Can we set specific targets with regard to senior employment rate in the growth industries?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme
sections.summary: Asks which industries the new programme will focus on and how long training will be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: On the new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme, which will replace the SGUnited Skills Programme and the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme, can the Ministry elaborate on which industries will it focus on and how long will the training be for?

sections.label: NTUC Company Training Committees funding
sections.summary: Asks what resources support the $100 million for NTUC to scale up Company Training Committees and transformation grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Chairman, in the Budget, $100 million has been set aside to support NTUC to scale up the Company Training Committees (CTCs) and introduce new grants to support company transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: What is the resource to support this and how will NTUC work with CTC to render the transformation support?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In 2008, the minimum qualifying period was reduced from six to three months, with the entitlement adjusted on a pro-rated basis.

sections.label: Fixed-term contract workforce share
sections.summary: States 8.4% of the workforce was on fixed-term contracts in 2021, up from 7.7% in 2009.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In 2021, 8.4% of the workforce was on fixed-term contracts, up from 7.7% in 2009.

sections.label: Paid sick leave proposal
sections.summary: Proposes amending legislation so workers completing one month of service get two days paid sick leave and eight days hospitalisation leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: When this happens, they are treated as a new employee requiring them to forgo paid sick leave for the first three months of the new contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I wish to propose that legislation be amended to allow workers who complete one month of service to be entitled to two days of paid sick leave, eight days of hospitalisation leave.

sections.label: Workplace fatalities in 2021
sections.summary: States 2021 saw 37 workplace fatalities, a steep rise from 30 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, 2021 saw 37 tragic workplace fatalities, a steep rise, compared to 30 fatalities in 2020.

sections.label: Liability for sub-contractor safety
sections.summary: The speaker proposes holding developers and main contractors jointly liable for poor WSH practices of sub-contractors on their sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This begets the question – why are the good safety practices not being filtered down to the sub-contractors?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I propose that we hold developers and main contractors jointly liable for poor WSH practices of sub-contractors working on their sites.

sections.label: Employment Act amendment date
sections.summary: The last round of Employment Act amendments took effect from 1 April 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The last round of Employment Act amendments was effective from 1 April 2019.

sections.label: Review of Employment Act
sections.summary: The speaker says it is appropriate to review the Employment Act or related labour legislation to address issues arising from gig work and other matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Considering these developments, I think it is appropriate to review the Employment Act or related labour legislation again to better address the plethora of issues arising from gig work, workplace fairness, whistle-blowing, treatment of sick leave and MCs, grievance handling, workplace harassment and discrimination, hours of work and overtime work, hybrid work, leave classification and contractual termination of workers without giving of termination reasons.

sections.label: Gig worker legislation and minimum earnings
sections.summary: The speaker asks if legislation will protect gig workers with minimum benefits and safety nets, noting a provision for local workers to earn at least $1,400 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Malaysia is also looking into a need for gig worker regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask the Ministry if legislation will be introduced to protect the rights of gig workers and provide them with at least the minimum levels of benefits and protection and safety nets, such as insurance and work injury compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: While not named a minimum wage per se, this provides for local workers with, at least, the ability to earn a minimum of $1,400 per month.

sections.label: Including gig workers in WICA
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry will consider including gig workers in WICA for mandatory protection while doing their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider including them in WICA so that the gig workers will have mandatory protection while doing their jobs?

sections.label: Gig workers' injury and CPF gaps
sections.summary: The passage states that under today's classifications, delivery riders' work injuries are not compensated on a national standardised level and employers' CPF contributions are not provided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Under today's classifications, work injuries, which our delivery riders are more at risk of, will not be compensated on a national standardised level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Employers' CPF contributions, which contribute to a significant portion to meeting requirement and housing needs, are also not provided.

sections.label: CPF savings for platform workers
sections.summary: The passage recognises the importance of sufficient CPF savings for basic needs and seeks clarification on how CPF will be shared between platform and workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In particular, we recognise the importance of having significant and sufficient CPF savings to meet basic needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We seek clarification on how CPF will be shared between the platform and the workers.

sections.label: PME jobs and new citizens
sections.summary: The passage states that 380,000 PME jobs for locals from 2005 to 2020 is unlikely to have benefited Singaporeans because over 635,000 new citizens and PRs were added.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We have previously pointed out that while the Government has insisted that the 380,000 PME jobs created for locals between 2005 and 2020 have benefited Singaporeans, that is highly unlikely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is because more than 635,000 new Citizens and PRs were added to the "locals" statistics during the same period.

sections.label: PME job shortage for graduates
sections.summary: The passage estimates a shortage of 100,000 to 150,000 PME jobs for Singaporeans over the last 20 years, excluding those demoted due to discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, not enough jobs are created for the 250,000 fresh Singaporean University graduates who joined the job market from 2005 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We can estimate that there is a shortage of 100,000 to 150,000 PME jobs for Singaporeans in the last 20 years, not counting those who were demoted due to discrimination.

sections.label: Workers unable to go out
sections.summary: The passage states that while the December update allows up to 3,000 workers out daily, workers are often not able to go out on workdays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the December update allows up to 3,000 workers out daily, workers are often not able to go out on workdays.

sections.label: Dorm vaccination rate and restrictions
sections.summary: The passage states that the vaccination rate among dorm residents is 98% and that this ought to be considered in easing movement restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The vaccination rate among dorm residents is 98% and that ought to be a consideration in easing movement restrictions.

sections.label: Retention Scheme matching period
sections.summary: The passage states that the Retention Scheme gives eligible workers 30 days to match with a new employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An exception is the Retention Scheme, which gives eligible workers 30 days to match with a new employer.

sections.label: Breastfeeding breaks laws study
sections.summary: A 2020 study of 97 countries found 82% had laws for paid and unpaid breastfeeding breaks, while Singapore does not legislate them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: A 2020 study of 97 countries found that 82% of countries had laws for paid and unpaid breastfeeding breaks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Singapore is in the minority of 18% of countries studied that do not legislate breastfeeding breaks.

sections.label: Budget support for workers and SMEs
sections.summary: The Budget apportions $600 million for the Productivity Solution Grant and $100 million to scale up CTCs, and extends the Progressive Wage Model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: In this Budget, we have apportioned significant resources, such as $600 million for the Productivity Solution Grant and $100 million to scale up CTCs to support transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: How can we get business associations to get more SMEs involved?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) will be extended and wage increases for low-wage workers will be co-funded under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: The qualifying monthly income cap for the scheme has been raised, age eligibility has been extended and the payout increased, especially for people with disabilities.

sections.label: Household Services Scheme history
sections.summary: The Household Services Scheme was first piloted in 2017 and made permanent in 2021, and has been welcomed by families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: The Household Services Scheme (HSS), first piloted in 2017 and made permanent in 2021, has been a popular and innovative scheme welcomed by families.

sections.label: Expanding Household Services Scheme to caregiving
sections.summary: The member invites the Ministry to look into expanding the Household Services Scheme beyond housekeeping into caregiving support for families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: There is also a great deal of untapped potential within the HSS to serve our residents better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Hence, I invite the Ministry to look into expanding the programme beyond the provision of housekeeping services into offering caregiving support for our families.

sections.label: Hybrid work and worker mental wellbeing
sections.summary: The member asks if the Government has guidelines safeguarding workers' mental wellbeing, citing a 2021 survey where over 80% of teachers reported hurt mental health.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Given that hybrid work arrangements are likely to stay and for good reason, I would like to ask if the Government also set in place guidelines and policies that safeguard the mental wellbeing of our workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: In a 2021 survey by Singapore Counselling Centre, more than 80% of teachers surveyed say that their mental health has been hurt by the pandemic.

sections.label: MOM support for mental wellbeing
sections.summary: The member asks MOM to update on plans to support employees' mental wellbeing at work and persons with mental health conditions returning to work.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Can MOM update on the plans to better support employees' mental wellbeing at the workplace and to support the employment and recovery of persons with mental health conditions transitioning back to work?

sections.label: Hybrid workplace legislation and mental well-being
sections.summary: The speaker says legislating hybrid workplaces is not tenable now and welcomes the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being guidelines on after-hours communications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: I understand that the legislation of hybrid workplaces is not the most tenable at the moment, lest we impose too many restrictions on businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: I am glad that the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being introduced guidelines for employers to set reasonable expectations for after-hours work communications.

sections.label: Portugal after-hours contact prohibition
sections.summary: In Portugal, employers are prohibited from contacting employees after office hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: For example, in Portugal, employers are prohibited from contacting employees after office hours.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements and worker surveys
sections.summary: Firms have made flexible work arrangements part of their new normal, and surveys show nearly 80% of workers want this flexibility continued post-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Many firms have made FWAs a part of their new normal, such as working from home, staggered hours and compressed work weeks and varying work duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Indeed, surveys have shown that nearly 80% of our workers hope that their employers will continue offering this flexibility in a post-pandemic age.

sections.label: FWA suitability and inclusive growth
sections.summary: Reports suggest PMET occupations suit flexible work arrangements more than frontline and shift work, and inclusive growth should create opportunities for seniors, workers with special needs, back-to-work mothers and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: For instance, various reports have suggested that occupations in the PMET sector are more suited for FWAs since their work hinges on more access to technology than physical interaction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: However, FWAs have been more difficult to implement in industries that need it the most, especially frontline workers and employees involved in shift work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Chairman, inclusive growth should create opportunities for seniors, workers with special needs, back-to-work mothers and those with caregiving responsibilities.

sections.label: Common HR industry accreditation proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a common accreditation for the HR industry, similar to an NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce recommendation on improving HR standards for fair employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: My proposal is to have a common accreditation for the HR industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This will set the foundation for workers' future work arrangement as companies respond differently to this new reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This proposal bears similarity to one of the recommendations by the NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce on enhancing fair employment practices through improving HR standards.

sections.label: MOM guidelines and Employment Act updates
sections.summary: MOM should consider framing clear guidelines and updating the Employment Act for such practices with SBF, SNEF, NTUC and HR professional associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: MOM should consider framing clear guidelines and consider updates to the Employment Act for such practices, in partnership with SBF, SNEF, NTUC and the various HR professional associations.

sections.label: HR-as-a-service idea
sections.summary: Asks whether an HR-as-a-service, similar to IMDA's CTO-as-a-service, would be worth considering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would a HR-as-a-service, similar to IMDA's CTO-as-a-service, be worth considering?

sections.label: Evolving HR value guidelines
sections.summary: States HR's value is fast-evolving and calls for guidelines on FWAs, mental health, SMEs, foreign manpower and agency engagement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: HR has always been important, but the nature of its value is fast-evolving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is the time to set guidelines for FWAs, enforce workplace mental health wellness, engage SMEs for deeper capability building, design strategic conversations for foreign manpower choices and encourage our relevant Government agencies, such as ESG and WSG, to triple-down in their joint engagements for results.

sections.label: IHRP certification support
sections.summary: Urges MOM to support and increase take-up of IHRP certification for human capital and HR professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: One of the key recommendations from the NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce report is to enhance fair employment practices through improving the human capital/HR standards among the human capital and HR professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge MOM to seriously consider supporting and increasing the take-up of the Institute of Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) certification for these professionals.

sections.label: Human Capital Partnership Programme update
sections.summary: Asks MOM for a progress update on the HCP Programme, its enhancement plans, and review of the HCP Mark criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The Human Capital Partnership (HCP) Programme is a tripartite initiative that brings together a community of exemplary employers in Singapore who have progressive employment practices in their organisations and are committed to developing their human capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I wish to ask MOM for a progress update of the HCP since the start of the programme and what are its plans to further enhance and make the programme even more pervasive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Does the award of the HCP Mark demonstrate that these employers are employers of choice who value their people and are committed to investing and developing their employees across all levels?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I am asking whether there will be a regular review of the key qualifying criteria for the HCP Mark and whether those awarded the Mark can have their mark removed if they fail to meet the criteria.

sections.label: Resident income and unemployment
sections.summary: States median gross monthly income of residents rose above pre-COVID-19 levels and unemployment fell to 3.2%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Despite a slight dip in 2020, the median gross monthly income of residents has risen to above pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Resident unemployment rate has come down from the high of 4.8% to 3.2% today.

sections.label: 2021 total employment rebound
sections.summary: States total employment rebounded by 40,800 for the full year 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the full year 2021, total employment saw an encouraging rebound of 40,800, close to 41,000.

sections.label: MOM priorities three Ups
sections.summary: MOM's priorities will focus on the three "Up"s: Upgrade, Uplift and Uphold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, MOM's priorities will focus on the three "Up"s: Upgrade, Uplift and Uphold.

sections.label: Uplifting vulnerable and mature workers
sections.summary: MOM will implement recommendations from the Tripartite Work Group on Lower-Wage Workers to uplift vulnerable and mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Hence, our second focus is to uplift our vulnerable workers and mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will implement the recommendations from the Tripartite Work Group on Lower-Wage Workers and double down on our efforts to uplift these workers.

sections.label: Jobseekers placed and funding allocated
sections.summary: Over 174,000 local jobseekers were placed into jobs and skills opportunities by end-December 2021, with $11 billion allocated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: More than 174,000 local jobseekers have been placed into jobs and skills opportunities as at end-December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: All in all, a total of $11 billion has been allocated to support these initiatives.

sections.label: EP minimum qualifying salary revised
sections.summary: EP minimum qualifying salary rises from $4,500 to $5,000, and from $5,000 to $5,500 in Financial Services, from September 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The EP minimum qualifying salary will be revised from $4,500 to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the Financial Services sector, which has higher wage norms, this will be revised from $5,000 to $5,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To give businesses sufficient time to adjust, these changes will apply to new EP applications from 1 September 2022 and to renewal applications from 1 September 2023.

sections.label: New COMPASS framework introduced
sections.summary: MOM will introduce COMPASS, a points-based system evaluating individual and firm-related attributes for EP applicant complementarity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is something that MOM has considered and studied carefully for quite some time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are now ready to introduce a new Complementarity Assessment Framework, called COMPASS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: COMPASS is a points-based system that considers both individual and firm-related attributes to holistically evaluate an EP applicant's complementarity.

sections.label: Two-stage EP framework
sections.summary: The future EP framework has two stages: meeting the qualifying salary and scoring sufficient COMPASS points.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With the introduction of COMPASS, the future EP framework will comprise two stages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, applicants must meet the EP qualifying salary.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Second, they must also score sufficient points under COMPASS, in order to qualify for an EP.

sections.label: COMPASS foundational criteria
sections.summary: COMPASS assesses EP applications on salary, qualifications, firm nationality diversity, and support for local employment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Under COMPASS, EP applications will be assessed based on four foundational criteria: (a) the candidate's salary relative to local PMET wages in their respective sectors; (b) the candidate's qualifications; (c) the firm's nationality diversity and whether the candidate improves the firm's nationality diversity; and (d) the firm's support for local employment compared to their industry peers.

sections.label: Bonus points C5 C6
sections.summary: Bonus points, termed C5 and C6, will be given in two areas where allowing the candidate serves Singapore's interest.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In such cases, it would be in Singapore's interest to allow the firm to bring in this candidate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we will accord bonus points for these two areas – these are termed C5 and C6.

sections.label: Smaller firms scoring exemption
sections.summary: Firms with fewer than 25 PMETs are automatically scored as meeting expectations on firm-related attributes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We recognise that for smaller firms, their workforce ratios can change significantly and drastically with only a few personnel changes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, for this practical reason, firms with less than 25 PMETs will automatically be scored as "meeting expectations" on firm-related attributes.

sections.label: COMPASS implementation dates
sections.summary: COMPASS takes effect for new EP applications from 1 September 2023 and renewals from 1 September 2024, with the rubric published on MOM's website.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We recognise that the introduction of COMPASS is a significant change and companies will need sufficient time to adjust to it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, COMPASS will come into effect for new EP applications from 1 September 2023 and for renewal applications from 1 September 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Following this announcement, we will publish the COMPASS scoring rubric on MOM's website.

sections.label: Global Rotation Scheme pilot
sections.summary: The Global Rotation Scheme is being piloted to facilitate entry of high-potential foreign employees, with companies posting local Singaporeans abroad in return.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will make sure that our EP framework has the flexibility to allow for such rotations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Therefore, we are piloting the Global Rotation Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This scheme will facilitate the entry of high-potential employees from abroad.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But, in return, these companies must also post our local Singaporeans abroad on the same leadership development programme.

sections.label: S Pass salary increase
sections.summary: S Pass minimum qualifying salary rises from $2,500 to $3,000, and to $3,500 for Financial Services, from 1 September 2022 for new applications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As a first step, we will raise the S Pass minimum qualifying salary from the current $2,500 to $3,000 and introduce a higher S Pass qualifying salary for the Financial Services sector at $3,500.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: These changes will be implemented for new applications from 1 September 2022 and for renewal applications from 1 September 2023.

sections.label: S Pass levy rate increases
sections.summary: MOM will raise the S Pass Tier 1 levy from $330 to $650 in three steps, while Tier 2 stays at $650.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: MOM will also progressively increase the S Pass Tier 1 levy rate from $330 to $650 over three steps, again, in tandem with the S Pass qualifying salary increases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It will be raised to $450 in September 2022 and then to $550 in September 2023 and $650 in September 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Tier 2 levy rate will be maintained at $650.

sections.label: Higher salary for renewals
sections.summary: The higher qualifying salary will apply only to EP and S Pass renewals in September 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, the higher qualifying salary will only apply to EP and S Pass renewals in September 2023.

sections.label: Raising salaries and levies
sections.summary: After weighing options, MOM raised both qualifying salary and levies to safeguard good employment outcomes for locals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I hope that we do not let perfection be the enemy of the good.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: That is why, after weighing our options carefully, we moved – raising both the qualifying salary and the levies to safeguard good employment outcomes for our locals.

sections.label: Construction and Process sector changes
sections.summary: From 2024, MOM will reduce construction and process sector DRCs from 1:7 to 1:5 and dismantle the MYE framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To support these transformation efforts, we will make further changes to the foreign workforce policies for the Construction and Process sectors from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, we will reduce the Dependency Ratio Ceilings, or DRCs, for the construction and process sectors from 1:7 to 1:5, to nudge the sectors towards reducing reliance on migrant workers and improving the productivity of workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Second, we will dismantle the Man-Year Entitlement (MYE) framework, to reduce allocation inefficiencies.

sections.label: M-SEP scheme launch
sections.summary: MOM is supporting MTI and economic agencies to launch the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To support the growth of businesses that contribute to Singapore's strategic economic priorities, MOM is supporting MTI and participating economic agencies to launch the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities, or M-SEP scheme.

sections.label: NTS Occupation List for Work Permits
sections.summary: MOM will let Services and Manufacturing firms hire some S Pass holders on Work Permits and introduce an NTS Occupation List.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With the moves to increase the benchmark for S Pass quality, MOM will allow businesses in the Services and Manufacturing sectors to hire some of these S Pass holders on Work Permits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will introduce a Non-Traditional Source (NTS) Occupation List, which is a tight list of rank-and-file occupations where employers will be allowed to hire NTS foreign workers on Work Permits.

sections.label: Business support measures funding
sections.summary: Support measures will provide up to $6.8 billion to businesses in financial year 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our support measures will provide up to $6.8 billion to businesses in financial year 2022.

sections.label: Foreign worker hiring flexibility
sections.summary: Firms in Services and Manufacturing may hire non-traditional Work Permit workers for selected occupations, and MOM will support a scheme giving extra quotas to strategic firms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For example, currently, some firms are unable to hire foreign workers they need due to certain Work Permit restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will allow firms in the Services and Manufacturing sectors to hire their workers from non-traditional sources on Work Permits, for a tight list of occupations with fewer locals, for example, in Precision Engineering and Food Manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: MOM will also support MTI in introducing a scheme to give additional S Pass and Work Permit quotas to firms that contribute to Singapore's strategic economic priorities.

sections.label: SME salary support for jobseekers
sections.summary: SMEs can enjoy up to 90% salary support to hire mid-career local jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: SMEs can enjoy up to 90% salary support to hire mid-career local jobseekers.

sections.label: Basic Retirement Sum adjustment
sections.summary: The Basic Retirement Sum will be adjusted to give higher monthly payouts, with about eight in 10 active CPF members turning 55 in 2027 expected to receive it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, we will adjust the Basic Retirement Sum to provide members with higher monthly payouts to keep pace with long-term inflation and rising standard of living.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We expect more members to receive at least the Basic Retirement Sum payout, with about eight in 10 active CPF members turning age 55 in 2027 being able to do so.

sections.label: CPF wage ceiling review
sections.summary: The CPF wage ceiling will be reviewed, with employers and employees engaged ahead of any changes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The CPF wage ceiling has been periodically updated since 2003 to keep pace with wages of resident workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will review the CPF wage ceiling and engage employers and employees ahead of any changes.

sections.label: CPF Investment Scheme outcomes
sections.summary: 75% of CPF Investment Scheme members made profits or broke even in FY2020, meaning 25% made cumulative total losses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As Mr Louis Chua mentioned, 75% of CPF Investment Scheme members made profits or broke even in the reporting period of FY2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This means that 25% of members made cumulative total losses.

sections.label: CPF retirement investment scheme study
sections.summary: CPF monies should be safeguarded for retirement, and a lifetime retirement investment scheme is being studied for members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we have to be very careful when striking this balance, because it involves CPF monies which should be safeguarded for retirement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are also studying if a lifetime retirement investment scheme can be introduced for members.

sections.label: Choppier waters fishing metaphor
sections.summary: Courses, upgraded equipment and COMPASS will help catch harder-to-catch fish despite choppier waters, with workers, unions, businesses and Government on the same ship.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Well, the essence of what we have laid out today reinforces this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But it also acknowledges that the waters are choppier, the fishes are harder to come by and catch, and if we just stay put and do not shift our anchor, we will soon run out of time and opportunity to fish!

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we will have courses to teach you how to catch the harder-to-catch fish, we will equip you with upgraded equipment – all the advanced rods, the sonar equipment – to fish, including using the new COMPASS to guide you to bountiful sources of fish, notwithstanding choppier waters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With workers, unions, businesses and the Government on the same ship together, I have no doubt that Singapore will continue her voyage into an even brighter future!

sections.label: National Jobs Council job placements
sections.summary: The National Jobs Council's efforts placed more than 174,000 local jobseekers into jobs and skills opportunities as at end December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The National Jobs Council's efforts saw more than 174,000 local jobseekers placed into jobs and skills opportunities as at end December 2021.

sections.label: JGI extension and salary support
sections.summary: The JGI will be extended six months from March 2022 to September 2022, with up to 40% then 20% salary support and up to $21,600 per hire.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: JGI-eligible employers have continued to hire from a wide pool of jobseekers, including half who were not employed at the point of hire.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will extend the JGI by another six months from March 2022 to September 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the next phase of the JGI, employers of these groups of jobseekers will receive up to 40% salary support for the first six months, and up to 20% for the next six months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In line with previous JGI phases, employers should achieve local workforce growth and growth in local workforce earning at least $1,400 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This means that eligible employers may receive up to $21,600 per hire over a 12-month period.

sections.label: Mature trainee allowance funding changes
sections.summary: Mature trainees keep allowances up to $3,800, but Government funding is scaled back from 90% to 70%, with host organisations co-funding 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Mature trainees will continue to receive training allowances of up to $3,800.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: However, with the recovery of the labour market, we will scale back Government funding from 90% to 70%, with the host organisations co-funding 30% of the allowance to the jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To encourage host organisations to hire the trainees earlier if they are found to be a good fit, we will allow host organisations to receive the full support quantum if the trainees were hired at least three months into the attachment.

sections.label: Workforce Singapore CCP placements
sections.summary: Since 2016, Workforce Singapore has placed over 39,000 locals into new job roles through CCPs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Since 2016, Workforce Singapore has placed over 39,000 locals into new job roles through CCPs.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs placement partners
sections.summary: Adecco was appointed as an SGUnited Jobs and Skills Placement Partner in March 2021, with Charterhouse and Good Job Creations appointed this month, and SGUnited Traineeships will not be extended after March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We appointed Adecco as an SGUnited Jobs and Skills Placement Partner in March 2021 and have appointed two additional employment agencies, Charterhouse and Good Job Creations, this month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will not extend the SGUnited Traineeships after it expires in March 2022.

sections.label: Scaling up CTCs
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said in the Budget speech that support will be given to NTUC's efforts to scale up to 2,500 CTCs by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has shared in the Budget speech that we will support NTUC's efforts to scale up to 2,500 CTCs by 2025.

sections.label: Raising retirement and reemployment ages
sections.summary: From July this year, the statutory retirement age rises from 62 to 63 and the reemployment age from 67 to 68, to let more senior workers work longer if they wish.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To allow more senior workers to work longer if they wish to, from July this year we will raise the statutory retirement age from 62 to 63 and the reemployment age from 67 to 68.

sections.label: Enhanced Workfare for lower-income SEPs
sections.summary: As announced at Budget 2022, eligible lower-income SEPs can receive enhanced Workfare payouts of up to $2,800 from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As announced at Budget 2022, eligible lower-income SEPs can receive enhanced Workfare payouts of up to $2,800 from 2023.

sections.label: Platform workers' CPF views
sections.summary: More than half of platform workers who responded to the public consultation felt mandatory CPF contributions to their Special or Ordinary Accounts would be important for retirement and housing needs, and the IPS survey found 84% worried about having enough retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: More than half of platform workers who responded to our public consultation exercise felt that mandatory CPF contributions to their Special or Ordinary Accounts would be important for their retirement and housing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And on this issue, the IPS survey found that 84% were worried about whether they have enough savings for retirement.

sections.label: Phased CPF contributions for platform workers
sections.summary: The Committee is considering requiring platform companies to make CPF contributions for platform workers' retirement and housing needs, and is considering a phased approach given companies' concerns about sudden business cost increases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Committee is considering the idea of requiring platform companies to make CPF contributions to support the retirement and housing needs of platform workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Platform companies have raised concerns that such a move will result in a sudden increase in business cost, something which I can understand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: So, an option being considered is a phased approach which will allow time for the platform ecosystem to adjust.

sections.label: Migrant worker vaccination and recovery
sections.summary: As of 20 February 2022, 99.4% of dormitory migrant workers were fully vaccinated, with fewer than 0.1% requiring hospitalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As of 20 February 2022, 99.4% of migrant workers residing in dormitories are fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Most experienced mild or no symptoms and were able to recover safely in recovery facilities, with fewer than 0.1% requiring hospitalisation.

sections.label: Community visits and testing step-down
sections.summary: Vaccinated migrant workers may go on community visits, over 95,000 have done so, and from 18 February the Rostered Routine Testing requirement was stepped down.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Vaccinated migrant workers are allowed on community visits and, as of mid-February 2022, more than 95,000 migrant workers have visited the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: From 18 February, we have also stepped down the requirement for migrant workers to undergo the Rostered Routine Testing, or RRT.

sections.label: Workers through Onboard Centres
sections.summary: To date, more than 55,000 workers have gone through the Onboard Centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To date, more than 55,000 workers have gone through the Onboard Centres.

sections.label: Review of dormitories act coverage
sections.summary: MOM is reviewing the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act to expand its coverage to smaller dormitories with fewer than 1,000 beds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOM is also reviewing the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act (FEDA) to expand its coverage to smaller dormitories with fewer than 1,000 beds.

sections.label: Primary Care Plan for migrant workers
sections.summary: From 1 April this year, employers will be required to purchase a Primary Care Plan for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On the outpatient front, as announced on 19 February 2022, employers will be required to purchase a Primary Care Plan, or PCP, for migrant workers with effect from 1 April this year.

sections.label: Primary Care Plan fixed fee
sections.summary: Employers can purchase the PCP at a fixed fee of between $108 and $138 per worker per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Employers can purchase the PCP at a fixed fee of between $108 and $138 for each worker per year, or about $9 to $12 per worker a month.

sections.label: Co-payment and claim limit
sections.summary: A co-payment component will be introduced for them, up to an annual claim limit of at least $60,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: A co-payment component will be introduced for them, up to an annual claim limit of at least $60,000.

sections.label: Insurer and employer co-pay
sections.summary: For the remaining $55,000, the insurer will co-pay 75% while the employer will pay the remaining bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For the remaining $55,000, the insurer will co-pay 75% while the employer will pay the remaining bill.

sections.label: Calibrated enhancements for medical bills
sections.summary: The enhancements have been carefully calibrated to provide better support for businesses and migrant domestic worker employers in managing large medical bills while keeping premiums affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The enhancements have been carefully calibrated to provide better support for businesses and migrant domestic worker employers in managing large medical bills while keeping premiums affordable.

sections.label: Migrant worker activities and Recreation Centres
sections.summary: Mr Lingam often accompanies residents requiring hospital treatment, and eight Recreation Centres offer programmes and activities, with a ninth ready later this year in Sembawang.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On top of his regular activities and duties, such as conducting briefings to fellow migrant workers on the latest Government advisories and guidelines, Mr Lingam often goes above and beyond by accompanying residents who require medical treatment at hospitals even when these incidents take place at night.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We are working with NGO partners to make our eight Recreation Centres livelier by bringing in more programmes and activities that our migrant workers enjoy, such as retail bazaars as well as sports and cooking competitions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: A ninth Recreation Centre will be ready later this year in Sembawang.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Workers are able to visit the Recreation Centres for essential services like topping up and purchasing telephone cards, going to the barber, buying groceries as well as for other recreational activities, such as movie screenings, live performances and meeting their friends.

sections.label: Adjusting migrant worker visit quota
sections.summary: Today, the visit slots are not fully utilised, but we are prepared to adjust the quota to allow more migrant workers to visit the community as the COVID-19 situation improves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Today, the visit slots are not fully utilised, but we are prepared to adjust the quota to allow more migrant workers to visit the community as the COVID-19 situation improves.

sections.label: PM Lee accepts workgroup recommendations
sections.summary: In his National Day Rally speech last year, Prime Minister Lee accepted the recommendations by the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in his National Day Rally speech last year, Prime Minister Lee accepted the recommendations by the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers.

sections.label: Lower-wage worker income growth
sections.summary: Real median income rose 2.1% annually while the 20th percentile rose 2.7%, with PWM and LQS seen as narrowing inequality.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Real median income of full-time employed residents has increased steadily at 2.1% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In comparison, real income at the 20th percentile – our lower-wage workers – has risen faster than median at 2.7% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Our moves to enhance wage growth in the PWM sectors and introduce the new Local Qualifying Salary, or LQS, provide us with further opportunities to narrow income inequality in the coming years.

sections.label: Entry-level cleaner wage increase
sections.summary: From 2022 to 2028, entry-level cleaners will see cumulative wage increases of up to 84%, reaching about $2,400 in 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For example, from 2022 to 2028, entry-level cleaners will see a cumulative wage increase of up to 84%, to receive baseline wages of about $2,400 in 2028.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary and PWM expansion
sections.summary: From September, the Local Qualifying Salary, Retail PWM and extended PWM take effect, covering 234,000 lower-wage workers by early 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Starting in September this year, we will implement the new Local Qualifying Salary requirement, as well as the Retail PWM and the extension of PWM to cover in-house cleaners, security officers and landscape workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Overall, by early 2023, 234,000, or more than eight in 10 full-time lower-wage workers will be covered by Progressive Wages.

sections.label: PW Mark for government suppliers
sections.summary: From March 2023, all suppliers awarded Government contracts must be accredited with the PW Mark, starting with larger-value contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From March 2023, we will require all suppliers awarded Government contracts to be accredited with the PW Mark, starting with contracts with larger value.

sections.label: Progressive Wages coverage total
sections.summary: Together the Progressive Wage measures raise coverage to 266,000, or 94% of full-time lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Chairman, putting our Progressive Wage measures together, this increases our coverage of Progressive Wages further up to 266,000, or 94% of full-time lower-wage workers – put together, 94%.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme co-funding
sections.summary: The Government will co-fund recent wage increases up to $2,500 from 2022 to 2026, with a second tier covering $2,500 to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: First, the Government will co-fund the first two most recent years of wage increases given to resident workers up to a wage ceiling of $2,500, for a five-year period from 2022 to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Co-funding will be at 50% in the first two years, 30% in the next two years, before tapering off at 15% in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With economic conditions remaining uncertain in the immediate term, the PWCS will also provide a second tier of funding to cover those earning between $2,500 and $3,000, for a shorter period of three years.

sections.label: Workfare payouts over fifteen years
sections.summary: Almost a million workers have received over $8.6 billion in Workfare payouts over fifteen years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Fifteen years on, almost a million workers have benefited from over $8.6 billion dollars in Workfare payouts.

sections.label: Workfare qualifying income cap raised
sections.summary: Workers earning up to $2,500 a month can now qualify for Workfare, up from $2,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Workers earning up to $2,500 a month will now be able to qualify for Workfare, up from the current qualifying income cap of $2,300.

sections.label: Older workers and PwD payouts
sections.summary: Older workers receive up to $4,200 a year, and from 2023 all PwDs are placed on that highest tier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Older workers, like Mdm Timah, will continue to receive the highest Workfare payouts, of up to $4,200 a year or $350 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From 2023, with the enhancements, we will provide a stronger helping hand by placing all PwDs on the highest payout tier of $4,200 a year.

sections.label: Workfare payouts for workers aged 30 to 34
sections.summary: From 2023, workers aged 30 to 34 can receive up to $2,100 in Workfare payouts a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From 2023, workers aged 30 to 34 like Ms Lily, many of whom are just starting their families or supporting elderly parents, can expect to receive up to $2,100 Workfare payouts a year.

sections.label: More lower-wage workers benefit from Workfare
sections.summary: From 2023, over half a million lower-wage workers will benefit from Workfare, up from 460,000 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Overall, the enhancements will benefit more workers, over half a million lower-wage workers from 2023 will benefit from Workfare, up from 460,000 today.

sections.label: Security PWM earnings
sections.summary: Under the Security PWM, Mr Ali will earn $3,550 per month in 2024 and entry-level officers at least $3,530 by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With the new recommendations for the Security PWM, Mr Ali will earn $3,550 per month in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Members may also be pleased to know that under the PWM, entry-level Security Officers will earn at least $3,530 by 2028.

sections.label: HCP Programme employer awards
sections.summary: Since 2017, the HCP mark has been awarded to over 600 employers employing more than 210,000 locals, about 10% of the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since the launch of the HCP Programme in 2017, we have awarded the HCP mark to more than 600 employers, who employ over 210,000 locals, or about 10% of the total local workforce.

sections.label: Progressive wages coverage 2023
sections.summary: By early 2023, 234,000 full-time lower-wage workers, over 8 in 10, will be covered by progressive wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: By early 2023, 234,000, or more than 8 in 10 full-time lower-wage workers will be covered by progressive wages.

sections.label: Government spending on two schemes
sections.summary: The Government will spend $9 billion over the next five years on the Progressive Wage Credit scheme and enhanced Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Overall, the Government will spend $9 billion over the next five years on these two schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The Government will spend $9 billion over the next five years for the Progressive Wage Credit scheme and enhance Workfare.

sections.label: Women's employment rate growth
sections.summary: The employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 grew from 73.2% in 2020 to 75.1% in 2021 despite the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The employment rate for women aged 25 to 64 has been growing over the past two decades and continues to grow from 73.2% in 2020 to 75.1% in 2021, despite the pandemic.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements continuation
sections.summary: In 2021, 73% of companies with flexible work arrangements said they were likely to continue them post-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2021, 73% of companies that adopted flexible work arrangements said they were likely to continue offering them post-COVID-19.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard adoption rate
sections.summary: One in four employees today work in companies that have adopted the Tripartite Standard.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Today, one in four employees work in companies that have adopted the Tripartite Standard.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements legislation caution
sections.summary: The speaker cautions against an overly rigid approach to legislating flexible work arrangements, which risks disputes and affecting employability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: On the idea of legislating flexible work arrangements brought up by Mr Louis Chua and Mr Yip Hon Weng, we should be careful not to take an overly rigid approach that risks creating a litigious workplace culture with more disputes, or inadvertently affecting the employability of the people whom we seek to help.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements resources and White Paper
sections.summary: Companies are encouraged to use available resources, with more details on ramping up flexible work arrangements in the coming White Paper.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: I encourage companies to make use of these resources that are available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We will be sharing more details on how we will ramp up provision of flexible work arrangements in the coming White Paper on Singapore Women's Development.

sections.label: Leave provisions and flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Members suggested more leave, but the speaker says increasing leave should not be the default and cites costs to businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng suggested raising minimum annual leave entitlements, introducing parent care leave and increasing parental leave provisions, while Mr Gerald Giam and Ms Mariam Jaafar spoke about sick leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We regularly review our leave provisions and acknowledge the real needs underpinning the Members' suggestions, but increasing leave provisions should not be the default solution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We have been advocating the adoption of flexible work arrangements precisely because they are flexible and able to cater to all forms of individual needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We should also recognise that there is a cost to increasing leave provisions and we must balance this carefully against what businesses can sustain in order to avoid dampening jobs growth.

sections.label: Medical certificate for sick leave
sections.summary: The Tripartite Partners' position is that employees should produce a Medical Certificate when using sick leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Partners' current position is the employees should produce a Medical Certificate (MC) when utilising sick leave, this helps to deter malingering and maintain a more disciplined workforce.

sections.label: Broadening HSS scope
sections.summary: The scope of HSS will be broadened to include basic child-minding and elder-minding services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To better help Singaporeans balance their work and family commitments, we will broaden the scope of HSS to include basic child-minding and elder-minding services.

sections.label: HSS expansion implementation timeline
sections.summary: MOM will engage stakeholders over the next few months and aims to implement the HSS expansion in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: MOM will also be conducting engagements with the stakeholders, such as households and HSS companies to work out the implementation details over the next few months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We aim to implement the HSS expansion in the second half of this year.
